reason: This is the Song of Moses (Exodus 15), a celebratory hymn commemorating the Israelites' deliverance from Egypt and the destruction of Pharaoh's army at the Red Sea. The text celebrates God's triumphant salvation and protection of the people rather than depicting them as suffering due to their own fault. The only suffering described is that of the Egyptians/Pharaoh (whose chariots were cast into the sea), presented as God's enemies. The Israelites are portrayed as recipients of God's mercy and redemption. The passage emphasizes divine intervention and God's promise to lead the redeemed people to His holy sanctuary—a narrative of salvation, not self-inflicted suffering.
